core_claim: Audient's third-generation iD interfaces add RoomTune monitor correction and onboard DSP effects.
topic: How Audient's third-generation iD interfaces measure room acoustics, adjust monitor playback, and run input effects through onboard DSP.
title: Can Your Room Trick Your Violin Mix?
hook: Could your room change your violin mix?
description: Audient's third-generation iD interfaces add RoomTune monitor correction. The system measures the listening environment and creates correction profiles for monitor outputs. The onboard DSP also runs EQ, compression and reverb in hardware without DAW latency. This Short illustrates monitor correction and input processing, not a claim that the original violin recording is rewritten.
cover_payoff: Use an original 2D editorial illustration of a complete violin and bow to demonstrate the monitoring signal path. Show the room-correction signal reaching the studio monitors, not rewriting the original recording. A sampled violin phrase is illustrative accompaniment and must never be presented as Prince's live performance.
narration_script: Could your room change your violin mix? Modern audio interfaces feature RoomTune monitor correction. It measures your room's acoustics and adjusts monitor response. Onboard DSP also runs input EQ, compression and reverb with no latency.

narration_evidence.quote: The real headline has a name, RoomTune. It is acoustic correction that measures the room’s response and adjusts your monitoring
It measures your room and adjusts the signal going to your monitors to compensate for its acoustics
The DSP also handles EQ, compression and reverb on the inputs with no latency and no load on your computer.

sources.title: Audient iD MK3: specs, release date and the RoomTune room correction

scenes.caption: YOUR ROOM CAN FOOL YOUR MIX.
scenes.image_prompt: A vivid, highly readable 2D editorial studio illustration in vertical 9:16. Put a full-size, unmistakably accurate amber-varnished violin in the foreground, with its classic upper and lower bouts, pinched C-bouts, two f-holes, ebony fingerboard, carved scroll, exactly four tuning pegs, exactly four strings, maple bridge and tailpiece. Place two clear studio monitors and a calibration microphone in the background. Use natural maple amber, warm walnut, ivory, graphite, teal and a restrained coral accent; preserve bright natural wood colour and clear subject separation. Strong first-frame silhouette, confident light direction, no text, no logos, no watermark, no generic lute silhouette, no extra tuning pegs, no CGI or 3D rendering.

scenes.caption: MEASURE. CORRECT. LISTEN.
scenes.image_prompt: A vivid, technically clear 2D editorial diagram scene in vertical 9:16. Show a calibration microphone centred between two recognisable studio monitors, with a single clear signal route and an illustrative response curve. Use distinct high-contrast colours for measurement, DSP correction and corrected monitor playback: cyan, coral and fresh green, with natural warm metal and wood details. Keep every connector straight, aligned and attached to its intended node. No numerical measurement claims, no text, logos or watermark, no CGI or 3D rendering.

scenes.caption: Room correction changes monitor playback—not the recording.
scenes.image_prompt: A vivid premium 2D editorial violin performance scene in vertical 9:16. Feature a clearly recognisable, anatomically accurate four-string violin in natural amber maple varnish, with the correct upper and lower bouts, narrow C-bouts, two f-holes, ebony fingerboard, carved scroll, exactly four tuning pegs, bridge, tailpiece and bow hair contacting the strings. Studio monitors remain clearly visible behind it. Use warm wood, natural ivory, rich teal, muted coral and clean neutral highlights; do not bury the instrument in a dark blue-black grade. No readable text, logos, watermark, generic lute or guitar silhouette, no extra tuning pegs, no CGI or 3D rendering.
